Completeness check

Possible missing data

The available files do not establish whether this was the final, complete copy of the system. If the recovered totals are consistent with expectations, no additional search may be necessary. If they appear low, the following areas may have additional data elsewhere.

Support calls

Call metadata may be incomplete

The yearly narrative files are present, but the table that linked each call to a customer, date, status and representative is not in this copy.

Equipment

The equipment master is not present

Equipment exports survive and contain at least 3,729 installation records. A later or more complete system copy may contain additional installations or updates.

Customer notes

References exist without note content

Many customer records contain note references, but the associated note content was not found in the supplied folder.

Financial history

No receivables records were found

Customer accounting identifiers are present, but the available receivables table is empty. Detailed history may have remained in ACCPAC rather than this system.

If the recovered totals appear lower than expected

The most useful additional item would be the latest complete copy of the application folder from the system where Service Call last ran. This means the entire folder containing SC.exe, not SC.exe by itself.

Other potentially useful material, if readily available:

  • A backup or disk image of the former YMS application server, including any system identified as YMS_TS.
  • Older complete SC folder copies from workstations, network shares, external drives, CDs or backup media.
  • ACCPAC company-data backups, but only if invoice or receivables history is required.

The software does not need to be run. A copy that preserves the original folder structure, filenames and timestamps is preferable.

Internals

Technical discoveries

Confirmed from binary inspection of the supplied SC folder. Source code is not present; language and schema notes below are inferred from executable metadata, embedded paths, and on-disk file headers.

Application / binary format

Primary binary: SC.exe (202,496 bytes). MZ stub + New Executable (NE) 16-bit Windows image. NE linker version 5.60; target OS byte = 2 (Windows). Stub string: “This program requires Microsoft Windows.”

Companion 16-bit NE modules: DBDLL.DLL (117,936 bytes, same linker 5.60), DBMFIX.EXE. Bundled DOS utilities include BTRIEVE.EXE (“Btrieve/N Record Manager Version 5.00a”) and BUTIL.EXE. No Btrieve data files (.BTR/.DDF) were found; those tools appear unused by the surviving datastore.

Runtime on this archive: Win16. Crash log drwtsn32.log identifies workstation YMS_TS, Windows NT 4.0 build 1381, org “York-Med Systems Inc.” A modern otvdm / winevdm 0.8.1 tree is present to host Win16 on 64-bit Windows.

Language and toolchain

Application code is C++, not Clipper/Harbour source. Evidence: embedded compile paths under d:\src.win\sc\*.cpp, Microsoft C++ decorated names (?ClientNotes@@ZCHIIIJ@Z), and 16-bit CRT objects (windows\crt0.asm, wchkstk.asm, stubmain.asm). Linker 5.60 is consistent with Microsoft Visual C++ 1.5x for Windows 3.x / Win16.

Embedded translation units include:

  • sc.cpp, scwin.cpp, scstatus.cpp, screg.cpp
  • callreps.cpp, callstat.cpp, recall.cpp, overdue.cpp
  • contact.cpp, affil.cpp, equip.cpp, orders.cpp
  • scnotes.cpp (ClientNotes / ClientNotesLoad / ClientNotesPrint)
  • sysindex.cpp, security.cpp, updatear.cpp, sysini.cpp

Data access is a private library via d:\src.win\sc\..\lib\dbdll.h → DBDLL.DLL. Classes: DBAREA, DBMEMO, DBMACRO. NTX operations: NTXOPEN, NTXCREATE, NTXSEEK, NTXGO, NTXKEYINSERT, NTXKEYDELETE. English/French index-corruption strings are compiled in.

Logical schema (from SC.exe)

Tables named in the binary:

sc_cust   sc_affil   sc_calls   sc_equip
sc_ar     sc_ctrl    sc_order   sc_sft
sc_sort   SC_LOCKS

NTX index aliases named in the binary:

ntx_cust   ntx_affil   ntx_calls   ntx_equip
ntx_ar     ntx_order   ntx_sft     ntx_page

Reindex entry points: LPREINDEX, reindexInit, reindexAddKey, reindexToDisk, reindexFinish. ntx_page plus scnotes.cpp imply a paging/notes store for SC_CUST.NOTE_NUM (N, 8); 1,771 of 2,181 active customers have a non-zero pointer. That store is not in this copy.

Call-report merge maps (HNET.MRG, ISS.mrg) document SC_CALLS fields: REASON, OPEN_DATE/TIME/REP, CLOSE_*, ASSIG_*, RESOL_TYPE, TYPE, TEXT (memo pointer into yearly DBM). Equipment maps document SC_EQUIP: MODEL, SERIAL, DESC, INSTALLED.

On-disk DBF headers (this copy)

Magic 0x03 = dBASE III+ without .DBT. Language-driver byte 0x00. Payload is 7-bit ASCII. Deletion marker 0x20 active / 0x2A deleted. Files are named Copy of SC_*.DBF, not the live names the app expects.

  last update 2009-05-12
  header 769 B, rec 384 B, 2195 recs (2181 active / 14 deleted)

  INC_LISTS L1, NETWORK C30, COLOR_CODE N1, NOTE_NUM N8, HNET C8

  ARBALANCE N19.5, REFERENCE C20

DBM call-memo store

27 yearly files SC_1992.DBM … SC_2017.DBM (~2.32 GB). Sizes are exact multiples of 512 bytes. First 512-byte block is null-padded. dbmfix.txt defines truncation at (call_num + 1) * 512 and states the last valid call_num lives in sc_calls.dbf. Example: dbmfix sc_2000.dbm 27540.

SC.exe references SC_CALLS->TEXT. Later-era blocks contain structured prose (“Issue #:”, contact name, problem details). Block offset is a usable surrogate key if SC_CALLS.DBF is recovered later. Without that table, customer/date/rep/status joins are heuristic only.

SC_1980.DBM is an empty 512-byte stub. No 1981–1991 or 2018+ files. One zip, sc_2003.zip, contains only sc_2003.dbm.

Other formats / runtime notes

  • Mail-merge dictionaries: 50 .mrg files mapping SC_* fields to Word/label output (dbMerge / MEMOMERGE).
  • List exports: 175 .LST files, typically 5-digit customer ID + padded name.
  • Jet copies: Copy of SC_CUST.mdb / SC_CUST1.mdb (“Standard Jet DB”); customer table only.
  • FRESTORE.EXE strings: “Restore from QNX's FBACKUP” — older backup path, not a current dump.
  • No .NTX/.CDX/.MDX indexes in this tree. App expects them co-located with SC.exe (no hardcoded data drive in the binary).
  • Customer-side products referenced in support text, not stored here as databases: yms.win / Medical Desktop (dBase), Purkinje Dossier / DCI.EXE (Raima Velocis + BDE), RPMS.

Method

High-level extraction process

Source files remain unchanged. Original values are preserved beside normalized fields and source references.

Preserve source files

Open sources read-only and record file size and SHA-256 hash.

Validate file structures

Check dBASE headers, field descriptors, record lengths and deletion markers.

Parse supplementary exports

Load later email, phone and fax files while retaining each original source row.

Normalize comparison fields

Standardize names, postal codes, phones and emails without changing original values.

Match records conservatively

Merge deterministic matches and separate ambiguous or unmatched records for review.

Validate outputs

Confirm record counts, unique IDs, source links, hashes and SQLite integrity.

Observed result: 2,194 later contact rows were staged. 1,885 matched deterministically; 34 remained ambiguous and 275 remained unmatched. No uncertain match was silently folded into the directory.

Migration design

Recommended Zoho CRM structure

Import the recovered data into related Zoho modules rather than one flat Contacts file. Preserve the YMS customer ID as an external key.

Customer organization or medical practice

Accounts

Legacy Customer ID as a unique external ID; Account Name; address; phones; fax; ACCPAC code; status/source fields

Named office contacts and affiliated physicians

Contacts linked to Accounts

Split multi-name legacy fields only after review; retain the unmodified legacy contact string

Support tickets and narratives

Cases plus Notes

Case Subject, Origin, Status, opened/closed dates, legacy rep and narrative. Use Calls only for true telephone activities

Equipment installed at a customer

Custom Installed Equipment module

Link to Account; model, serial, description, install date and source. Use Products for the reusable product catalogue

Customer software and versions

Custom Installed Product module

Link Account to product/version and preserve snapshot date/source

Recall, newsletter and courtesy lists

Campaigns

Deduplicate recipients before import and retain the original source-list membership

Scope limits

Limitations

Missing call and equipment index tables limit complete relational reconstruction. The remaining exports still support targeted recovery.

Temporal limit

No single “current” snapshot

The customer master is from 2009; later exports enrich it but do not prove continued activity.

Call limit

The narrative index is missing

Most DBM text cannot be linked reliably to account, date and status from the available copy.

Inventory limit

The equipment master is missing

Overlapping flat exports must be normalized and deduplicated.

Financial limit

No receivables ledger available

The available table has zero records. ACCPAC customer identifiers remain, but balances and invoices do not.

Action required

Decisions and next steps

Work on extraction and Zoho preparation will wait on the choices below. A time estimate will be provided after the requested scope is confirmed.

Are the recovered totals complete enough?

If the counts in this report match expectations, we can proceed from the current copy. If they look low, upload the latest complete folder that contains SC.exe and send an email when the upload is finished.

Which data should go into Zoho CRM?

Please say which of these to include: customer accounts and contacts; affiliated physicians; equipment; installed software; support calls; campaign lists. We will quote time against the selected items only.

Should unmatched later-list names be included?

Some names appear only in later phone, fax or email lists and were not linked to the 2009 customer master. They can be held out, or brought in as additional customer candidates. They are not proof that those accounts were still active.

Start now, or wait for additional files?

If more SC files may still arrive, say whether quoting and extraction should wait. Otherwise we will work from what is already in hand.

What happens next

  1. Review this report and the contact sample.
  2. Reply with the four decisions above.
  3. Upload additional files only if the totals look incomplete, then email that the upload is done.
  4. We return a time estimate for the confirmed scope.

What we will do after that

  • Extract and clean only the data areas you select.
  • Prepare Zoho-ready import files for those modules.
  • Keep ambiguous and unmatched records in separate review files.
  • Leave the original SC files unchanged.
